sentences.text: Smt. Dr. Anjali Gyanani - Public Prosecutor for the res Heard on I.A. No.15985 of 2024, which is 1st application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant No.1- Vikram Anuragi.

2. This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 30.04.2024 passed by the 11th Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Gwalior, whereby the applicant has been convicted under Sections 376(DA), 376(3) of IPC and Section 3 read with Section 4 and Section 5(g) read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo life imprisonment with fine of Rs.10,000/-
under Section 376 (DA) of IPC.
3.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Prosecution story, in brief, is that on 27.4.2022 prosecutrix (PW-1) aged about 16 years was sleeping in her house and her mother (PW-3) was at shop and door of the house was open, at that juncture, applicant along with co-accused Gaurav Pawaiya and one juvenile accused entered the room of the prosecutrix, locked it from inside, took the prosecutrix to inner room and committed rape with the prosecutrix one by one.
The accused threatened her to kill if she narrated the incident to anyone.

On 23.5.2022 at about 9 pm accused persons came to the house of the prosecutrix and started quarreling with the mother of the prosecutrix as prosecutrix narrated the incident to her 2 CRA-6920-2024 mother.
The accused persons threatened to kill if report is lodged.

The prosecutrix by filing the written complaint (Ex.P/1) lodged the report (Ex.P/2) at police Station, University,
Distt. Gwalior, on which crime No.227/2022 was registered against accused persons under Sections 376D, 506 of IPC and Sections 3/4 of the POCSO Act.
After investigation, Challan was filed against the applicant and co-accused in the Special Court.
Charges were framed against the applicant which he denied and claimed for trial.
After trial, the Special Court on appreciation of evidence placed on record convicted and sentenced the present applicant as mentioned above.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

There is contradiction in respect of the age of the prosecutrix and Vikram Anuragi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24987306/
1 prosecution has failed to prove that on the date of incident prosecutrix was minor.

sentences.text: Prosecutrix (PW-1) and mother of the prosecutrix (PW-3) turned hostile and they did not support the story of prosecution.
Medical examination of the prosecutrix was conducted after much delay.
The evidence does not show that samples were taken and stored without any alteration which makes the DNA report highly unreliable.
The doctor who conducted DNA examination has not been examined.
Rajendra (PW-5) has denied that he has collected the sample of applicant which makes the process of entire DNA vitiated and unreliable.

While relying upon the SOP on collection & processing of scientific/ forensic evidences in case of sexual assault on women issued by the National Human Rights Commission, it is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that optimal time for forensic DNA evidence collection is 3 CRA-6920-2024 upto 72 hours (in no case beyond 96 hours)
of the assault.
However, forensic DNA evidence can still be collected upto 7 days due to advancements in DNA technology.
Here in this case, the date of incident is 27th April, 2022, sample was taken on 25.5.2022, kept in Malkhana upto 6.6.2022 and sent for DNA examination on 10.8.2022.

It is further submitted that as per DNA report (Ex.P/30), mixed Y- Chromosome STR DNA profile taken from vaginal slide has been matched with Y- Chromosome STR DNA taken from blood sample of the applicant, but at the same time, in Plazo and vaginal swab respectively, low and uninterpretable Y-Chromosome STR DNA profile was detected.
Since the vaginal slide was prepared out of vaginal swab, therefore, that also renders doubt on the veracity of the DNA report (Ex.P/30).
It is further submitted that co-accused Gaurav Pawaiya has been granted bail by this Court on 29.07.2024.
On these grounds, it has been prayed that the applicant may be extended the benefit of suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

5 . Per contra, learned counsel for the State while supporting the judgment impugned submits that no exception can be taken in the matter of suspension of sentence and grant of bail, regard being had to the nature and the gravity of offence found proved against the present applicant.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
Prosecutrix (PW-1) and her mother (PW-3) turned hostile and did not support the story of prosecution.
As per their statements, prosecutrix was 19 years of age in the year of incident.
They categorically denied that birth certificate reveals her true date of birth.

Her mother (PW-3) also stated that 4 CRA-6920-2024 she did not get birth certificate (Ex.P/5) prepared, therefore, so far as date of birth of the prosecutrix on the date of incident is concerned, contrary evidence is on record.

Co-accused Gaurav Pawaiya has been granted bail by this Court on 29.07.2024.
8.

Considering the evidence on record and the period after which sample has been sent for analysis,
without commenting on the merits of the case, I.A.No.15985 of 2024 filed by applicant Vikram Anuragi stands allowed and it is directed that the jail sentence of applicant shall remain suspended during pendency of the present appeal and he shall be released on bail subject to verification of the factum of depositing the fine amount and on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
